export_note: Selected fields from the completed native grade; machine-local paths are omitted. The mathematical grade is preserved.

grade.first_issue: From \(H\cap P_i=\{p\}\) and \(P_i\cap P(m)\ne\varnothing\), it does not follow that \(p\in P(m)\); the prime in \(P_i\cap P(m)\) may lie outside \(H\).
grade.summary: The solution correctly reduces the problem to eventual stabilization of the admissible sets and gives a sound periodicity argument conditional on that stabilization. However, the central proof that only finitely many minimal hitting sets can occur relies on a false inference, so stabilization is unproved. Repairing this requires the main nontrivial finiteness argument.
strengths: Correctly describes each finite-stage admissible set as a finite union of divisibility classes.
The final deduction from stabilization to translation-periodicity is essentially correct.

errors.description: The claimed containment \(H\subseteq H_N\cup P(m)\) is unsupported because the witness argument does not force \(p\in P(m)\); consequently, finiteness of the possible \(\mathcal H_n\) and stabilization of \(S_n\) do not follow.
A nondecreasing sequence of positive integers need not stabilize merely for being positive; boundedness should be stated using \(a_1\in S_n\), which gives \(m_n\le a_1\).
The claim that earlier \(a_i\) remain in \(S_n\) does not follow from \(S_n\subseteq S_{n-1}\) alone, though it is routinely repaired using symmetry of the gcd condition with \(a_n\).
